# BAD-069 — deno check writes an ungitignored deno.lock at the repository root

## Brief
`deno check` on an Edge Function writes `deno.lock` at the repository root, and nothing ignores it. Confirmed on the BAD-047 worktree: `check-ignore -v deno.lock` matches nothing, and `.gitignore` names no deno entry at all.

That matters now because BAD-047 makes `deno check` part of the routine: the spike's section 8a runs it on every commit of the split as the type-error baseline, and anyone verifying a future Edge Function change will run it too. Russet hit it on pass 1 and deleted the file by hand, which is the fix that does not survive the next person.

Two ways to settle it, and the choice is a real one rather than a formality:

- **Ignore it.** Add `deno.lock` to `.gitignore`. Right if the lockfile is an artifact of a local check and nothing more — which is what it is today, since no CI job runs `deno check` and the deploy bundles the import graph server-side.
- **Commit it.** A lockfile pins the `npm:postgres@3.4.5` resolution that `_shared/db.mjs` pulls, which is the one third-party dependency the functions have. That has value, but it is a new thing for this repo to maintain and nothing currently reads it, so it should be a deliberate decision rather than a side effect of someone forgetting to delete a file.

Recommend ignoring it unless there is an appetite for pinning, since a lockfile nobody reads is a file that rots.

Raised by BADS-047/Russet as an open question during BAD-047 pass 1; filed by Spud after confirming it is genuinely untracked and unignored.

## Size, persona and model decision
One scout on haiku, or a line in whatever PR next touches .gitignore; the only judgement is whether a lockfile is wanted at all.
